page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.4-64 is a flexible virtual machine instance configured with AMD EPYC processors and an expanded memory footprint. The instance allocates 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7742 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.25 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled. CPU resources are dedicated rather than shared, ensuring consistent compute execution without resource contention from neighboring tenants.

The memory configuration provisions 64.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a 1:8 ratio of vCPUs to memory (8.0 GB per vCPU). This elevated memory allocation positions the instance within the memory-optimized spectrum, providing substantial headroom for memory-intensive execution paths. The instance does not include integrated local storage or discrete GPU hardware, requiring external block volume attachments for persistent storage and file systems. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included for external network access.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the flexible sizing model enables high memory capacity without forcing the provisioning of unnecessary compute cores, reducing overhead for memory-bottlenecked deployments. The primary operational trade-off is the reliance on remote storage solutions for disk I/O. This hardware profile is appropriate for in-memory caching systems, mid-tier database management engines, enterprise Java applications, and memory-bound data analysis pipelines.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.4-64 is a flexible compute instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7742 processor running at 2.25 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 physical cores mapped across 8 dedicated vCPUs with two threads per core. The server features 64.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-dense execution. The instance includes no hardware GPUs and lacks bundled local storage, depending entirely on networked block storage for persistent data access. Network connectivity includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. With dedicated CPU allocation and an elevated memory ratio, the instance provides steady compute performance while catering to memory-heavy workloads without requiring additional compute provisioning. It fits in-memory caching nodes, relational and NoSQL databases, memory-constrained container clusters, and data processing tasks requiring substantial RAM alongside moderate core counts.
